title: Man. Post. Cap. IX: even if actual — entered by venom, not imputation
pass_a_gloss: Grant the sense for a moment; I still deny entry into the world by imputation. 'Entered' means he left his venom in Adam, and without that kind of reckoning it crept Adam→Seth→Enosh→Kenan and so by degrees father to sons until it reached us by natural begetting and increase.
pass_b_english: Grant nevertheless that it is so understood; I will deny that that sin entered into the world by imputation. Rather it is said to have entered into the world, because he left his venom in Adam, which without that kind of imputation crept from Adam into Seth, from Seth into Enosh, from him into Kenan, and so little by little flowed from father into sons, until it reached us by natural propagation and multiplication.
source_text: Fac tamen intelligi; negabo peccatum illud introiisse in mundum per imputationem: sed dici introiisse in mundum, quia suum venenum reliquit in Adamo, quod sine eiusmodi imputatione serpsit ab Adamo in Sethum, à Setho in Enosch, ab hoc in Kenanem, & ita paulatim à patre in filios manavit, donec ad nos perveniret propagatione & multiplicatione naturali.

choices.choice: Entered = venom left; natural line Seth–Kenan, not imputation

notes: Cap. IX names densify section 487 from locked 1661 Latin (pp. 318–320 tip).
